# Your savings

## The idea

Every self-tax Aevum charges you moves real money into a savings account. This is
the part of Aevum that keeps the books on that account — so at any moment you can
see how much you've set aside, and where it came from.

It isn't a number Aevum invents. It's a running record of actual money you've moved
out of your everyday spending and into savings, kept honestly enough that you can
always trace any figure back to the payment behind it.

## What you'll see

The Savings view answers one simple question: **how much have you set aside, and how
solid is it?** It splits your balance into two kinds of money:

- **Recognized savings** — money you've paid that's matched to a bill you owed
  yourself. This is settled: a tax you levied on your own spending, now funded.
- **Received in advance** — money you've moved across ahead of any bill. It still
  counts toward your balance; it just hasn't been claimed by a specific bill yet.
  As new bills come due, this is drawn down to cover them.

Alongside the balance you get a **week-by-week trend** of how your set-aside total
has grown over time, so the habit is something you can watch, not just a snapshot.

## Always up to date

You never have to wait for anything to "run." Every time you open your savings,
Aevum re-reads what you've actually paid and what you owe yourself, and reconciles
the two on the spot. The balance you see is always current with your latest activity.

Because the record only ever gets _added to_ — never quietly rewritten — your savings
history stays trustworthy. If something changes (a payment is undone, a bill
reopens), Aevum posts a correcting entry rather than editing the past. You can trust
that what you saw last week is still what happened last week.

## Savings today, more tomorrow

Today this is exactly what it sounds like: **a savings account** — real money, set
aside, yours. That framing is deliberate. The balance you build here is the
foundation the rest of Aevum is designed to grow on.

In time, that same set-aside balance is meant to do more than sit still — it's the
starting point for putting your savings to work. The account you're funding now is
the one those later features will build on. For now, though, it does the most
important thing first: it holds your savings safely, and shows you the truth about
them.
